title: NF-kappaB signaling is the major inflammatory pathway for inducing insulin resistance.
authors: Mobeen, Ahmed; Joshi, Sweta; Fatima, Firdaus; Bhargav, Anasuya; Arif, Yusra; Faruq, Mohammed; Ramachandran, Srinivasan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究NF-kappaB信号通路在胰岛素抵抗中的作用，基于基因表达和通路模拟，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Insulin resistance is major factor in the development of metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes (T2D). We extracted 430 genes from literature associated with both insulin resistance and inflammation. The highly significant pathways were Toll-like receptor signaling, PI3K-Akt signaling, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, pathways in cancer, TNF signaling, and NF-kappa B signaling. Among the 297 common genes in all datasets of various T2D patients' tissues including blood, muscle, liver, pancreas, and adipose tissues, 71% and 60% of these genes were differentially expressed in pancreas (GSE25724) and liver (GSE15653), respectively. A total of 169 genes contain highly conserved motifs for various transcription factors involved in immune response, thereby suggesting coordinated expression. Through co-expression analysis, we obtained three modules. The respective modules had 78, 158, and 55 genes, and TRAF2, HMGA1, and RGS5 as hub genes. Further, we used the BioNSi pathways simulation tool and identified the following five KEGG pathways perturbed in four or more tissues, namely Toll-like receptor signaling pathway, RIG-1-like receptor signaling pathway, pathways in cancer, NF-kappa B signaling pathway, and insulin resistance pathway. The genes NFKBIA and IKBKB are common to all these five pathways. In addition, using the NF-kappaB computational activation model, we identified that the reversal of NF-kappaB constitutive activation through overexpression of NFKB1 (P50 homodimer), PPARG, PIAS3 could reduce insulin resistance by almost half of its original value. To conclude, co-expression studies, gene expression network simulation, and NF-kappaB computational modeling substantiate the causal role of NF-kappaB pathway in insulin resistance. These results taken together with other published evidence suggests that the TNF-TRAF2-IKBKB-NF-kappaB axis could be explored as a potential target in combination with available metabolic targets in the management of insulin resistance. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s13205-024-04202-4.
abstract_zh: 胰岛素抵抗是代谢综合征和2型糖尿病（T2D）发生的主要因素。我们从文献中提取了430个与胰岛素抵抗和炎症相关的基因。高度显著的信号通路包括Toll样受体信号通路、PI3K-Akt信号通路、细胞因子-细胞因子受体相互作用、癌症通路、TNF信号通路和NF-kappa B信号通路。在来自不同T2D患者组织（包括血液、肌肉、肝脏、胰腺和脂肪组织）的所有数据集中共有的297个基因中，分别有71%和60%的基因在胰腺（GSE25724）和肝脏（GSE15653）中差异表达。共有169个基因包含多种参与免疫反应的转录因子的高度保守基序，从而提示协调表达。通过共表达分析，我们获得了三个模块。各模块分别有78、158和55个基因，并以TRAF2、HMGA1和RGS5作为枢纽基因。此外，我们使用BioNSi通路模拟工具，识别出以下五个在四个或更多组织中受扰动的KEGG通路，即Toll样受体信号通路、RIG-1样受体信号通路、癌症通路、NF-kappa B信号通路和胰岛素抵抗通路。基因NFKBIA和IKBKB是所有这五个通路共有的。另外，利用NF-kappaB计算激活模型，我们确定通过过表达NFKB1（P50同源二聚体）、PPARG、PIAS3来逆转NF-kappaB组成性激活，可将胰岛素抵抗降低至其原始值的近一半。总之，共表达研究、基因表达网络模拟和NF-kappaB计算建模证实了NF-kappaB通路在胰岛素抵抗中的因果作用。这些结果与其他已发表证据相结合，提示TNF-TRAF2-IKBKB-NF-kappaB轴可作为潜在靶点，与现有代谢靶点联合用于胰岛素抵抗的管理。补充信息：在线版本包含补充材料，可在10.1007/s13205-024-04202-4获取。
